Signet
rollout overview.

Signet’s initial rollout centers on IAM: establishing the shared operating system, preparing the first venture for controlled activation, and measuring what can be reused for the next. This overview sets out the implementation scope, operating responsibilities, release gates, and open decisions.

Planning draft · Phase owners, timing, funding, and release approvals remain to be confirmed.

Explore the rollout

Signet is owned by Obsidian Capital Partners. IAM is its first operating-company licensee.

What is Signet?

Autonomy, under seal.

Signet runs agentic brand systems for portfolio operators. Agents prepare the work, a named human gives the go, and Signet keeps the record.

Proof that a person said yes.

Every claim, spend change, piece of content, and launch gate has an accountable owner. A Record without a named sealer cannot be shown as sealed.

Prepared. Sealed. Recorded.

Agents prepare the work. A named person authorizes it. Signet preserves the decision and its evidence. Licensed providers retain clinical decisions.

Green means a named person gave the go. It never means selected, in progress, or ready for review.

Methods move. Identities stay separate.

Signet codifies IAM’s operating method once, as independent infrastructure. Approved methods and playbooks move between ventures; identities, rights, and sensitive data remain separate.

ObsidianOwns Signet and IAM

SignetBuilds and licenses the system

IAMForms and operates the ventures

One venture first.
Then a repeatable rollout.

Why the shared model works

IAM should not rebuild a company for every creator.

Build a portfolio of category-authentic health ventures on one shared commercial operating system. The stores feel different. The underlying launch, growth, measurement, and governance machinery compounds.

01
✦

Creator-led, not creator-dependent

Talent opens attention and trust. The company still needs product-market fit, clinical service quality, retention, and contribution economics.

02
↗

Shared engine, distinct ventures

Reuse the operating method and technical substrate—not another creator's identity, patient data, claims, or licensed content.

03
◎

Prove before multiplying

One category-authentic creator, one care pathway, and one measurable cohort before tier-one guarantees or a multi-store rollout.

PORTFOLIO VIEW

IAM allocates capital and operating attention across a venture portfolio.

Each venture has its own rights, P&L, clinical arrangement, customer relationship, and shutdown conditions. IAM reuses methods and infrastructure across the portfolio.

  • Talent underwriting and venture formation
  • Portfolio resource allocation
  • Shared commercial capabilities
  • Authorized aggregate intelligence
The boundary that protects the company: clinical decisions stay with licensed providers; commercial agents never become clinicians.

Launch cockpit

DELIVERABLE

READY WHEN

Content pipeline

DELIVERABLE

Approved brand, rights, and claims material with a traceable review path.

READY WHEN

Growth journey

DELIVERABLE

A consented path from approved education to licensed care and lifecycle support.

READY WHEN

Economics cockpit

DELIVERABLE

Care navigation

READY WHEN

Support coverage, clinical escalation, and incident handling are accepted.

How the rollout operates.

Agents prepare research, drafts, orchestration, monitoring, and analysis. Accountable people accept releases, spending, and operating decisions. The roles below describe the intended model; appointments and authority limits remain to be confirmed.

GROWTH POD

Turn approved audience hypotheses into measurable learning.

Segment audiences, draft experiments, monitor channel performance, and recommend reallocations without allowing an agent to publish or spend outside approved bounds.

AGENTS PREPAREHUMANS APPROVESIGNET RECORDSOUTCOMES TEACH

Signet delivers. IAM accepts and operates.

Signet configures the system, permissions, evidence records, and operating playbooks. IAM accepts the handoff, assigns operators, and owns venture execution. Licensed providers retain clinical decisions.

Proposed review rhythm: a readiness review before each release, daily exception review during controlled activation, and weekly operating and finance review. Confirm the participants and cadence before activation.

Escalation: pause the affected workflow, record the issue, and route it to the accountable operator or licensed clinical team. Resume only after the responsible authority records clearance.

The company learns.
The boundaries remain.

Signet is the governed system of work across IAM—not the EHR, not a cross-store health dossier, and not a replacement for accountable operators.

Launch gates and measurement.

Set metric definitions and decision thresholds before activation. Actual results and baselines have not been supplied for this draft. The review plan below is proposed for operator confirmation.

Readiness and rights

Proposed owner: IAM operating lead + counsel

Proposed cadence: At each release gate

Proceed, repair, or stop against the accepted evidence record.

Service and support

Proposed owner: Venture operator + clinical counterpart

Proposed cadence: Daily during activation

Resolve capacity, handoff, complaints, and escalation exceptions.

Acquisition and retention

Proposed owner: Growth lead + finance

Proposed cadence: Weekly; retention at D30 / D60 / D90

Assess appropriate acquisition and whether cohorts retain value.

Contribution and cash

Proposed owner: Finance lead

Proposed cadence: Weekly; settlement reconciliation

Reconcile all material costs, contribution, and cash received.

Replication readiness

Proposed owner: IAM + Signet leads

Proposed cadence: After first-venture evidence review

Transfer the method only when results and venture-two readiness support it.

We stop or repair if:rights are incompleteclinical capacity is uncleareconomics do not reconcileunsafe claims escape reviewtrust deteriorates

The boundaries for implementation.

  1. Clinical independence. Licensed providers control clinical decisions and care.
  2. Rights before replicas. No avatar use without specific, written, channel-level authorization.
  3. Evidence before scale. Capital, paid acquisition, and tier-one talent follow observed cohort economics.
